climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and Riesling fully without cooking off their freshness.
Pinot Noir is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Chardonnay is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. Chalk is soft, porous limestone. Roots push deep into it, and it drains well while still storing water. It is planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
